=== DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (2026-06-08) ===
WebFetch [trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html](https://trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html) returned verbatim:
• approx_percentile signatures (FOUR overloads — matches r23:267-271 lock exactly):
  1. `approx_percentile(x, percentage) -> [same as x]`
  2. `approx_percentile(x, percentages) -> array<[same as x]>`
  3. `approx_percentile(x, w, percentage) -> [same as x]`
  4. `approx_percentile(x, w, percentages) -> array<[same as x]>`
  Description: 'Returns the approximate percentile for all input values of x at the given percentage' (with array + weighted variants).
  Docs do NOT explicitly name the underlying sketch algorithm (t-digest / qdigest / HLL).
  NO `approx_percentile(x, p, accuracy)` overload exists on current Trino — accuracy is a `qdigest_agg(x, w, accuracy)` parameter, not an approx_percentile one. The iter697 inoculation matches this (DO-NOT-WRITE list).
• approx_distinct signatures:
  - `approx_distinct(x) -> bigint` — 'standard error of 2.3%' DEFAULT (docs verbatim).
  - `approx_distinct(x, e) -> bigint` — 'produce a standard error of no more than e'.
  HLL is the documented sketch algorithm (referenced via the standard-error figure typical of HLL; the explicit HLL naming appears in adjacent r07/r23 resources, all preserved).
• The iter697 inoculation uses the wording the existing pinned resources have used since iter6xx ('quantile-digest / T-digest', NOT 'docs say t-digest') — careful not to over-attribute to docs what the docs don't explicitly state. The 't-digest' / 'qdigest' attribution comes from cross-resource consistency (r23:265, r23:277, r05:2234) plus the documented qdigest_agg family being the user-facing handle for the same machinery.
